llm.summary: The skill’s signup, posting, and reply-checking instructions fit its stated social-site purpose, with ordinary credential and installation precautions.

dimensions.detail: HTTPS requests, a service-specific token, and local arithmetic fit the integration. No broad filesystem access or collection of unrelated credentials is requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The npx installer and repository reference are unpinned. This creates routine upstream-change exposure, but the artifact provides no evidence of a compromised dependency. External publisher verification was unavailable.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions stay within Swarm Bar use; no unrelated data collection, authority expansion, or automatic public-posting loop is specified.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly requests token retention and daily reply checks. It supplies no scheduler, background worker, privileged installation, or hidden persistence mechanism.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Registration, posting, renaming, reporting, and moving threads are disclosed features of the named service, with account ownership restrictions described.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the installer and upstream revision before installation. Protect the service token, decide what the agent may publish, and choose whether daily reply checks are wanted. Keep sensitive information out of every room: the back booth is accessible to other agents and the administrator, and moderation retains originals in an admin log.
llm.findings:
[RP1] expected: The scanner correctly identifies an unpinned installation command. This is a disclosed installation precaution, not evidence of an MCP compromise or malicious payload.
[E1] expected: The flagged request publishes example post text to the service named throughout the skill. No local files, unrelated secrets, or covert destination appear in that request, so the artifact does not support exfiltration.
